sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: During Q1 2026, overall plant defect rate averaged 3.8%, driven primarily by elevated nonconformance in Product Line B (HVAC Control Module) and Product Line D (Industrial Sensor Hub). These two lines accounted for 71% of all internal defects and 76% of customer returns recorded between January and March. Concentrated analysis identified three dominant failure modes responsible for the majority of scrap and warranty claims. Corrective actions implemented in March show measurable improvement in April production data.

sections.heading: Defect Rates by Product Line
sections.body: Product Line B reported a Q1 average first-pass yield of 92.4%, with solder joint voiding and intermittent power faults representing 5.1% of total units built. Product Line D posted a higher defect rate of 6.3%, largely due to enclosure seal leakage and calibration drift beyond ±1.5% tolerance. In contrast, Product Lines A and C remained stable below 1.2% defect rate, indicating issues were localized rather than systemic. Weekly trend analysis shows defect peaks in Weeks 4 and 9 corresponding to supplier lot changes.

sections.heading: Root-Cause Analysis of Top Failure Modes
sections.body: Cross-functional root-cause reviews conducted on 18 February and 12 March determined that solder joint voiding in Line B originated from inconsistent reflow oven temperature profiles after a preventive maintenance interval extension. For Line D, seal leakage was traced to dimensional variation in gasket material from Supplier KX Polymers, exceeding the specified compression set limit. Calibration drift was linked to an outdated firmware compensation algorithm not aligned with the latest sensor revision. These three failure modes accounted for 64% of Q1 customer return authorizations.

sections.heading: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Status
sections.body: CAPA-26-017 addressed reflow temperature instability through reinstatement of biweekly thermal profiling and operator retraining, fully implemented on 20 March. CAPA-26-021 required Supplier KX Polymers to revise tooling and submit enhanced SPC data; incoming inspection sampling was increased from AQL 1.0 to 0.65 pending qualification. CAPA-26-024 deployed firmware version 3.2.7 with updated compensation coefficients, validated through 500-cycle accelerated life testing. As of 25 April 2026, all three actions are verified effective with documented reduction in associated defect codes.

sections.heading: Customer Return Trends and Recovery Indicators
sections.body: Customer returns peaked in February at 412 units but declined to 238 units in March and 96 units in April month-to-date. Warranty claims related to solder faults decreased by 58% following reflow process stabilization, while seal-related returns dropped by 61% after containment of suspect gasket lots. April’s rolling defect rate for Lines B and D combined has improved to 1.9%, indicating recovery toward the plant target of 1.5%. Continued monitoring through Q2 will confirm sustained performance and prevent recurrence.

structure.full_text:
Q1 2026 Quality Performance and CAPA Status Summary
Ref: QLT-26-041 | Date: 28 April 2026 | From: Quality Systems Manager, North Valley Plant

Section Executive Overview
During Q1 2026, overall plant defect rate averaged 3.8%, driven primarily by elevated nonconformance in Product Line B (HVAC Control Module) and Product Line D (Industrial Sensor Hub). These two lines accounted for 71% of all internal defects and 76% of customer returns recorded between January and March. Concentrated analysis identified three dominant failure modes responsible for the majority of scrap and warranty claims. Corrective actions implemented in March show measurable improvement in April production data.

Section Defect Rates by Product Line
Product Line B reported a Q1 average first-pass yield of 92.4%, with solder joint voiding and intermittent power faults representing 5.1% of total units built. Product Line D posted a higher defect rate of 6.3%, largely due to enclosure seal leakage and calibration drift beyond ±1.5% tolerance. In contrast, Product Lines A and C remained stable below 1.2% defect rate, indicating issues were localized rather than systemic. Weekly trend analysis shows defect peaks in Weeks 4 and 9 corresponding to supplier lot changes.

Section Root-Cause Analysis of Top Failure Modes
Cross-functional root-cause reviews conducted on 18 February and 12 March determined that solder joint voiding in Line B originated from inconsistent reflow oven temperature profiles after a preventive maintenance interval extension. For Line D, seal leakage was traced to dimensional variation in gasket material from Supplier KX Polymers, exceeding the specified compression set limit. Calibration drift was linked to an outdated firmware compensation algorithm not aligned with the latest sensor revision. These three failure modes accounted for 64% of Q1 customer return authorizations.

Section Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Status
CAPA-26-017 addressed reflow temperature instability through reinstatement of biweekly thermal profiling and operator retraining, fully implemented on 20 March. CAPA-26-021 required Supplier KX Polymers to revise tooling and submit enhanced SPC data; incoming inspection sampling was increased from AQL 1.0 to 0.65 pending qualification. CAPA-26-024 deployed firmware version 3.2.7 with updated compensation coefficients, validated through 500-cycle accelerated life testing. As of 25 April 2026, all three actions are verified effective with documented reduction in associated defect codes.

Section Customer Return Trends and Recovery Indicators
Customer returns peaked in February at 412 units but declined to 238 units in March and 96 units in April month-to-date. Warranty claims related to solder faults decreased by 58% following reflow process stabilization, while seal-related returns dropped by 61% after containment of suspect gasket lots. April’s rolling defect rate for Lines B and D combined has improved to 1.9%, indicating recovery toward the plant target of 1.5%. Continued monitoring through Q2 will confirm sustained performance and prevent recurrence.

Confidential — Quality Review Copy | Page 1 of 1
